notes:
PASS on the fake backend: python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/labs/florianbauer__ot2-controller --backend fake exits 0; the report's evidence is contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level. The clone at eabc7fa6df1aea483d8438dbc540ccb3fffa6b67 was left unmodified and is never imported or run by the package. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card names family python-object / PythonObjectDriver, but this is a direct Driver over Ot2ControllerImpl because the only stop path closes the nested Paramiko SSHClient (native.ssh.close at ot2_controller/feature_implementations/ot2controller_impl.py:160), which a config-only PythonObjectDriver binding cannot express. COVERAGE: the primary interface is preserved as cap.process.run.v1 (recipe_ref is the uploaded protocol file name, dry_run selects opentrons.simulate versus opentrons.execute) plus the connection and available-protocols state reads. NOT COVERED: the built-in camera picture and camera movie (get_CameraPicture/get_CameraMovie) and the UploadProtocol/RemoveProtocol commands. cap.sensing.image.v1 requires numeric width, height and exposure inputs, while the upstream command always captures a fixed 640x480 JPEG and exposes no setting, so binding that class would require accepting inputs the device cannot honor. LIMITS: the driver has no numeric input and declares no Limit; there is therefore no site-limits.example.json overlay, and G8 reports the expected G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE warning because SAFE-014 has no actuating limit to probe (every other CL3 test passed). SAFETY: the clone has no stop, cancel, pause or abort method; the interactive stop stops the SiLA server process, not the OT-2 (ot2_controller/__main__.py:70-78). The @estop and the input-free safe-state action close the SSH transport, which ends the remote opentrons.execute/opentrons.simulate command stream but does not power off the OT-2 and does not prove that motion already commanded to the robot has stopped. estop_terminal is declared because the feature has only that one session and a new SSH connection/driver instance is needed afterwards; the driver has no @reset. No line of the clone documents an independent hardware e-stop, so estop_physical_ref is not set; the safe-state action satisfies SAFE-045 for this R2 driver and is not a substitute for the operator's hardware stop. FAKE: fake.py is a synthetic F0 stand-in, not a recording, not captured traffic and not the upstream simulator (the clone ships none). Its connection string, protocol name, run duration and polling interval are placeholders marked in the file; its RunProtocol models a short run and raises when the fake SSH transport is closed, so the close is observable, but that model is not evidence about a live OT-2. FIDELITY GAP: upstream get_AvailableProtocols filters readlines() lines with endswith('.py') while each line keeps its [...]

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the direct Driver against ot2controller_impl.py, ot2controller_base.py, __main__.py, README.md and doc/UserGuide.md at the pin, reproduced the author's pass (digest sha256:2984bd56...) and confirmed the predicted block: the upstream has no stop, cancel, pause or abort (ot2controller_base.py:12-94), and the author's e-stop and safe_state=True action x-cap.florianbauer.abort_protocol.v1 only closed the SSH client ('Close connection', ot2controller_impl.py:159-161) while RunProtocol starts python3 -m opentrons.execute with exec_command(cmd) (:116-119), which no line of the clone stops, so the SDK reported an achieved safe state for a disconnect, and estop_terminal described that disconnect although an SSH reconnection changes nothing on the device (CORE-087). Further defects: recipe_ref went unquoted into a root shell command (:114, :116); a non-zero executed exit status and a missing status (-1 after a closed channel) were completed receipts (CORE-071); cancellable=True answered 'cancelled' for a run that goes on to its end on the robot; four facts named things outside their cited ranges (root at :17; /data/user_storage/ at :18, twice; the server stop at __main__.py:70-78) and two said more than their lines (the newline-blind filter at :54 called a .py filter; the destructor's 'Close connection' called a stop); and the fake listed a protocol the upstream filter never returns. The reviewer changed driver.py (the e-stop closes the client, then raises SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED; the safe-state action and estop_terminal removed, so the author's catalogue request for x-cap.florianbauer.abort_protocol.v1 is obsolete; safe_state rewritten; recipe_ref limited to ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*\.py$; status 0 completes, any other status fails MHS.DEVICE.FAULTED with the native code, a missing status or a failure after the start is unknown; the run is not cancellable; both read descriptions corrected; facts split, narrowed and added, 11 to 16), fake.py (the upstream filter verbatim, -1 on a closed channel, the simulation ValueError, test knobs), native.py (unknown options are refused instead of being ignored, so a misspelt key option no longer falls back to the default key), test_driver.py (ten cases: the unreached e-stop with the latch held, an e-stop mid-run leaving the run unknown, refused names, return codes, a decode failure, a refused cancel; the stock gate case kept) and facts.md, and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json. The gate now fails only G3 SAFE-045 (no independent stop and no safe-state action; stable digest sha256:d0c156e6865249189cda9e498ab4024ad96be2c64616973e7dd11240bafb3dea), the ten package cases pass, the stock gate case fails as expected while blocked, and the author's notes describing a pass, the safe-state action, estop_terminal and the cancellable run are superseded. For the human reviewer: An R2 liquid handler that runs any uploaded protocol file (arbitrary Python, so whatever the robot and its attached modules can do, heating included) as root over SSH, with the calibration steps omitted (doc/UserGuide.md:82); a deployment with biological samples or heated modules may need R3. There is no stop: exec_command(cmd) (:119) requests no pseudo-terminal, and under usual SSH server behaviour (outside the clone) such a command is not signalled when the client disconnects, so after the e-stop the protocol may run to its end or fail at an unpredictable point on a later write to the closed channel (the author's log assumed sshd sends SIGHUP, which holds only with a terminal). Unblocking needs a stop of the running protocol whose effect is confirmed from source. Other hazards: unknown host keys are accepted automatically (AutoAddPolicy, :43) and the connection has no timeout (:45); RunProtocol prints the remote output on the host's stdout (:121-125), which would corrupt an MHS server on stdio, and reads all of stderr before stdout, so a large stdout may stall it; the protocol list is expected to be always empty (:54); protocol files are named, not content-addressed as the class note requires.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-sonnet-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Adversarial verification of the claude-opus-5-5 review (block) by a different model (the user chose Claude Sonnet as the different model, 2026-11-04): the verifier agreed and found no blocker or major. The block is genuine. The gate fails only G3, with SAFE-045 (R2 hardware device with no independent stop and no safe-state action). collect.py --strict reports FAIL G3 plus RESULT_UNTRUSTED, because RESULT.json still says pass. show_refs.py reports 0 bad citations, and the cited lines I read say what the Facts claim. The upstream has no stop, pause or abort method. The destructor's close (:159-161) leaves the remote opentrons.execute process running. Because the e-stop honestly raises SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED, the package has no hardware-free path to a stop, and NO_HARDWARE_FREE_PATH fits. I found no blocker or major issue the reviewer missed.
